result.title: Throwing4: Phase-Aware Pose Modeling for Throw-Distance Prediction in Elite Athletics
result.comment: Accepted for publication in Sports Engineering
result.summary: Elite athletics throwing provides a structured biomechanical action sequence together with an objective continuous outcome, namely throw distance, making it a suitable setting for performance-oriented sports analytics. In this work, we investigate whether explicit phase alignment of pose dynamics improves throw-distance prediction under realistic broadcast conditions. To support this study, we curate Throwing4, a dataset of 500 elite throwing clips spanning javelin, discus, hammer, and shot put, with corresponding two-dimensional pose sequences, frame-level phase annotations, and official distance labels. We formulate throw-distance prediction from broadcast-derived pose as a regression problem and compare full-sequence modeling against a phase-conditioned approach that partitions each attempt into four technique stages and fuses phase-specific motion representations. Experiments across multiple graph-based pose encoders show a consistent reduction in prediction error when phase structure is incorporated, indicating that phase-aligned modeling provides a more stable representation than treating the entire motion as an unstructured sequence. These findings suggest that explicit biomechanical phase information is a useful inductive prior for pose-based performance modeling in elite athletics throwing. Beyond score prediction, the dataset and protocol provide a basis for future work on fine-grained technique analysis, interpretable sports analytics, and robust modeling from broadcast video.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 Throwing4 数据集（500 段精英投掷视频的 2D 姿态序列、帧级阶段标注与官方距离标签），将广播姿态下的投掷距离预测建模为回归任务，并比较整段序列建模与按四个技术阶段划分、融合各阶段运动表示的相位条件建模。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但其「把连续运动切成固定阶段再融合阶段专属表示」的相位条件做法，可能为把推理轨迹分段、按阶段维护并融合 latent 状态的思路提供类比线索，可供核查；是否真的优于整体序列建模需读原文。
